cur:manuscripts-khludov-transfiguration.summary: At the top of a steep red mountain, Christ stands in a blue mandorla between Moses and Elijah, while on the slopes below the three apostles fall to the ground, dazzled by the light. The tall, narrow composition fits the margin of the page beside the psalm text it illuminates.
facts: Byzantine marginal psalters commonly attached the Transfiguration to the verse 'Tabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name' (Psalm 88:13 in the Septuagint).
The Khludov Psalter contains 169 folios and measures about 195 by 150 mm.
cur:manuscripts-khludov-transfiguration.notes: The specific psalm verse beside this miniature is not legible in the low-resolution image; the Tabor association is the usual one in this tradition.

cur:objects-berlin-crucifixion-with-sold.summary: Christ is crucified high in the upper part of the panel, with mourning angels above the cross. Below, the Virgin and the holy women stand at the left, while at the right a group of helmeted soldiers gathers. The fuller, more narrative version of Calvary contrasts the sorrow of the faithful with the indifference of the executioners.
facts: Byzantine ivory carvers produced both the simple three-figure Crucifixion and fuller narrative versions with soldiers and mourners, sometimes in the same workshop (type).
